questions.question: Draw or describe the four flows between households and government in the circular flow, and label each as a real flow or a money flow.
questions.expected_answer: Households to government: labour (real flow) and taxes, rates and service charges (money flow). Government to households: wages and salaries plus transfers such as social grants (money flow) and public goods and services such as schooling, health care, policing, water and roads (real flow). Real and money flows between the same two sectors run in opposite directions; grants are transfers with no real flow in return.

questions.question: Explain how government acts as a consumer and as a producer in relation to households. Give one example from each sphere for the producer role.
questions.expected_answer: Consumer: government buys the labour of household members by employing them, e.g. police and soldiers (national), teachers and nurses (provincial), refuse collectors and traffic officers (local), and pays salaries. Producer: government supplies goods and services to households, e.g. national — policing, identity documents, social grants through SASSA; provincial — public schools, hospitals and clinics; local — water, sanitation, electricity, refuse removal, street lights.

questions.question: State four responsibilities of households towards government. A household buys soap for R40 excluding VAT and maize meal for R60. Calculate the VAT paid on the two items.
questions.expected_answer: Pay taxes (PAYE income tax, VAT); pay municipal rates and service accounts; use resources such as water and electricity responsibly and protect public property; participate by voting and attending ward or IDP meetings. VAT: soap 15% of R40 = R6; maize meal is zero-rated, so R0. Total VAT = R6.
